facts.text: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) guidance on computational modeling for medical devices is final guidance published in November 2023 on assessing computer-model credibility in medical-device submissions.
facts.quote: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) published final guidance in November 2023 on assessing the credibility of computer models in medical-device submissions

facts.text: The booklet identifies the FDA guidance as the clearest regulator-level statement of starting simulation credibility assessment from the decision rather than from the simulator.
facts.quote: the booklet cites it as the clearest regulator-level statement of how to start from the decision rather than from the simulator.

facts.text: The FDA guidance builds on ASME V&V 40.
facts.quote: The guidance builds on ASME V&V 40

facts.text: The FDA guidance begins credibility assessment by defining the question of interest and context of use, then rating model risk as model influence combined with decision consequence.
facts.quote: First define the question of interest and the context of use. Then rate model risk as model influence combined with decision consequence.

facts.text: The FDA guidance calls for setting credibility goals before collecting evidence, then collecting evidence and judging its adequacy.
facts.quote: Then set credibility goals before collecting evidence. Then collect it (eight categories of evidence, within a nine-step process) and finally judge whether it is adequate.

facts.text: The FDA guidance uses eight categories of evidence within a nine-step process.
facts.quote: eight categories of evidence, within a nine-step process

facts.text: The FDA guidance specifies no universal minimum of physical, bench or clinical evidence; the evidence amount depends on risk and context.
facts.quote: There is no universal minimum of physical, bench or clinical evidence; the amount depends on risk and context

facts.text: Under the FDA guidance, model credibility applies to the stated context of use, not to every future application of the model.
facts.quote: credibility applies to the stated context of use, not to "the model" for every future application

facts.text: The FDA guidance covers only physics-based and mechanistic models, not data-driven models.
facts.quote: the guidance covers physics-based and mechanistic models only, not data-driven ones

facts.text: The FDA guidance requires validation thresholds to be justified for the decision and sets no universal acceptance error.
facts.quote: validation thresholds must be justified for the decision; it sets no universal acceptance error

facts.text: The booklet uses FDA logic to argue that the claim “simulation validates automatic braking” is too broad and must be split into separate testable claims.
facts.quote: The booklet uses the FDA logic to argue that "simulation validates automatic braking" is too broad a claim and must be split into separate testable claims

facts.text: The booklet lists prospective credibility goals among the items an assessor expects because these goals prevent changing the metric after inconvenient results.
facts.quote: it lists prospective credibility goals, which stop the metric being changed after inconvenient results, among the items an assessor expects
